question: World Health Organization (WHO) gave its Tobacco Control Award for the year 2019 to the health department of the Indian state of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) awarded the **Tobacco Control Award for 2019** to the health department of Rajasthan.
 
• This award is given in recognition of the state's efforts to implement strong tobacco control measures.
 
• Rajasthan's health department has been proactive in **promoting public health** and reducing tobacco consumption through various initiatives and programs.
 
• The award highlights the state's commitment to **creating a healthier environment** by combating the tobacco epidemic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Health Organization (WHO)**

 
 
• The WHO is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health.
 
• It was established on 7 April 1948 and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
 
• The WHO's primary role is to direct and coordinate international health within the United Nations system.
 
• Their main areas of work include health systems, promoting health through the life-course, noncommunicable and communicable diseases, and corporate services.
 
 
 
• **Tobacco Control Measures**
 
 
• Tobacco control measures are public health policies and initiatives aimed at reducing the prevalence of tobacco use and its health consequences.
 
• These measures include the implementation of smoking bans, increasing taxes on tobacco products, running public awareness campaigns, and providing support for smoking cessation.
 
• Effective tobacco control policies can significantly reduce the health burden caused by tobacco use, including diseases such as cancer, heart disease, and respiratory illnesses.
 
• Countries and states that implement strong tobacco control measures often see a decrease in tobacco consumption and related health issues.
 
 
 
• **Health Department Initiatives in Rajasthan**
 
 
• The health department of Rajasthan has implemented various programs to control tobacco use and promote public health.
 
• These initiatives include public awareness campaigns, school education programs, and strict enforcement of tobacco control laws.
 
• Rajasthan has also established tobacco cessation centers to help individuals quit smoking and other forms of tobacco use.
 
• The state's efforts in tobacco control are part of a broader strategy to improve overall health outcomes and reduce the incidence of tobacco-related diseases.
